ExploreFact.Text: A large structure built into the planet on the equator, some sort of dry dock for constructing space vehicles.

RumorFact.Text: A space station appears to be parked inside the drydock.

ExploreFact.Text: A space station is designed to be launched into a solar orbit to stabilise the sun, to prevent the destruction of the planet.
It only has half of the power requried to save the sun.
If two Sun Stabilisation Devices were launched in sync with each other, that would save the sun.

RumorFact.Text: I was told that there is some sort of temporal displacement device on the South pole of the planet.

The rules of time travel are different from what I am used to: when I change something on the younger planet, the changes instantly affect the older planet without me needing to wait a loop. In fact, if I die and loop, I will need to make the changes again.

ExploreFact.Text: A device on the South pole of the planet.
The planet disapears into a black hole about 15 minutes into the loop.
When the younger planet disapears into the black hole, it goes back in time to become the older planet that emerges from the white hole earlier into the loop.
The planet spontaneously appears from a while hole about 5 minutes into the loop.
This new planet is suspiciously similar to that other planet, though it seems older.

AltText.Text: This is the same planet as the other one, but from the future.

RumorFact.Text: Someone named Bruce is working on a sun stabilisation device. He can be found near the planet's equatorial dry dock.

ExploreFact.Text: Bruce is in charge of and vital to the Sun Stabilisation Project.
On the older version of the planet, Bruce is dead because some debris fell on the exact spot he was standing.
I was able to save Bruce's life by telling him to move 3 steps to the left, causing him to appear on the older planet.

RumorFact.Text: The Dry Dock's mechanism to launch the Sun Stabilisation Device is linked to the North pole's communications center.

ExploreFact.Text: Corey is on the North pole of the planet, a location which acts as the planet's observatory and radio communications center.
The North pole's radio communication equipment allows the past and future versions of the planet to communicate with each other.
